prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” HVAC company for every homeowner in Atlanta — the right contractor depends on your ZIP code, the size/age/type of your home and system, your budget, timing, and whether you want top-tier equipment/warranty or the best value.

I can find highly rated contractors for your exact neighborhood, but first here are practical guidelines and what I’d recommend you do to identify the best company for your AC replacement:

Quick questions so I can make a tailored recommendation
- What’s your ZIP code?
- Single‑family home or condo/apartment? Approx. square footage?
- Do you have existing ductwork (central AC) or a ductless system?
- Target timeline (ASAP vs. within a month)?
- Any budget or brand preference? Want top-efficiency (higher SEER) unit?

How to choose the best contractor
1. Get at least 3 written estimates that include: equipment brand & model, SEER rating, full scope of work, labor warranty, manufacturer warranty, removal/disposal, permit fees, and total price.
2. Require a proper load calculation (Manual J) — not just “match the old tonnage.” Proper sizing prevents comfort and efficiency problems.
3. Check credentials: Georgia ROC or local license number, proof of insurance, NATE-certified technicians, and local references. Verify reviews on Google, BBB, and recent customer photos/testimonials.
4. Ask about experience with the brand they’re selling and whether they handle warranty service themselves.
5. Compare the full installed system and the installation quality — duct sealing, line-set length, proper refrigerant charge, and correct airflow matter as much as the condenser.

Red flags
- High‑pressure door‑to‑door sales or “today‑only” discounts.
- Cash‑only deals without written contract.
- No Manual J or vague scope of work.
- No license/insurance or unwillingness to provide documentation.
- Extremely low bid that leaves out permit or replacement of necessary components.

Typical price range (Atlanta, ballpark)
- Replacement of a typical central AC unit (3–5 ton): roughly $3,000–$8,000 depending on equipment quality, SEER rating, duct work needed, and labor. High-efficiency or multi-zone systems cost more. Obtaining local quotes will narrow this.

What to ask each contractor
- Will you perform a Manual J? Can I see it?
- What SEER is this unit and what brand/model?
- Is the price for a matched system (evaporator coil + outdoor unit)?
- What warranty is provided (labor and parts)? Are extended warranties offered?
- Do you handle permits and city inspections?
- Do you provide a final system performance report (refrigerant charge, airflow)?

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and any of the details above and I’ll pull up 3–5 well‑rated, licensed HVAC contractors in your area and summarize their strengths, typical pricing, and recent review highlights.
